methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines clinical resistance profiling in 30 FGFR2-driven cancers treated with lirafugratinib, serial ctDNA/tissue analyses, RNA-seq/GSEA, Ba/F3 mutagenesis and viability assays, structural modeling, PDX pharmacology, and three clinical sequencing cases. This triangulation is well suited to identifying resistance mechanisms and testing drug complementarity. Limitations include small and heterogeneous clinical subgroups, incomplete post-progression tissue WES/RNA-seq, three different liquid biopsy panels, and PDXs that do not fully capture ctDNA polyclonality. Statistical methods include DESeq2/GSEA with FDR thresholds and an exact permutation test for mutation spectra, but many clinical and preclinical comparisons are descriptive without power calculations or confidence intervals.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: For Oxford classification, the evidence is level 5 because the central claims are mechanistic/translational, supported by molecular profiling, cell lines, PDX models, and a very small number of sequential-treatment clinical cases rather than a comparative clinical cohort or trial endpoint analysis. Clinical relevance is high because FGFR2-driven cholangiocarcinoma and other solid tumors have approved or emerging FGFR inhibitors, and resistance mutations directly inform sequencing of lirafugratinib and futibatinib. The three patients responding to futibatinib after lirafugratinib are compelling but not sufficient to establish clinical efficacy of the sequence.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the closest checklist because PDX experiments are central to the functional validation, although the manuscript also has clinical molecular profiling components. The manuscript reports patient inclusion criteria, trial/program identifiers, consent and ethics approvals, sequencing platforms and thresholds, RNA-seq/GSEA parameters, cell engineering, viability assays, PDX mouse strain, group size, dosing, and structural-analysis tools. Reporting is weaker for animal randomization/blinding, formal sample-size rationale, complete allocation/exclusion details, and harmonization across liquid biopsy panels. No public sequencing, expression, analysis-code, or PDX dataset repository is described in the normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper offers a novel resistance map for lirafugratinib, especially recurrent M538 and L618 mutations, and uses functional models to show complementarity with futibatinib. It is well positioned against prior resistance literature for reversible FGFR inhibitors and futibatinib, and it explicitly compares mutation spectra with published futibatinib data. Prior work already established polyclonal FGFR2 resistance and some sequential inhibitor concepts, so the novelty is strong but still an extension within an active precision-oncology niche rather than a wholly new paradigm.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is detailed and generally well organized, moving from clinical cohort to resistance categories, functional testing, structural rationale, and clinical sequencing examples. The abstract captures the major clinical, molecular, in vitro, in vivo, and patient-sequence findings. Figure captions are information-rich and help decode a complex multi-panel translational story. Some sections are dense, and the recommendation for clinical sequencing occasionally reads stronger than warranted by only three post-lirafugratinib futibatinib cases with intervening therapies.

key_strengths: Integrates clinical ctDNA/tissue profiling with in vitro, in vivo, structural, and patient-level sequencing evidence.
Identifies recurrent lirafugratinib resistance mutations at FGFR2 M538 and L618 residues.
Provides functional evidence that futibatinib can overcome key lirafugratinib resistance mutations in Ba/F3 and PDX models.
Explicitly compares resistance spectra for lirafugratinib and futibatinib to support rational sequencing.
key_concerns: Clinical cohort and sequencing cases are small and heterogeneous across tumor types and prior treatments.
Post-progression tissue WES/RNA-seq was incomplete, and liquid biopsy testing used three different panels.
The clinical evidence for sequential lirafugratinib-to-futibatinib use is limited to three patients, often with intervening therapy.
Animal randomization, blinding, sample-size rationale, and public data/code availability are not fully reported.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a strong translational precision-oncology study with coherent mechanistic and pharmacologic validation. Tier 2 with minor revisions is appropriate, mainly requiring tighter calibration of clinical sequencing claims and fuller reporting of animal rigor and data availability.
